title: Codex Ultimus: Restored, Badly
statement: Kite pulled five tiles out of my grid and left them in a heap. A conservator came after, and I was the conservator. Four tiles are back in their cells, each turned the wrong way, their glyph lines running vertical where the neighbours run horizontal, and each join is filled with a bright seam of the archive's memory gold so the repair is visible from across the room, as a good repair should be. The fifth cell I left open on purpose: the one with sky behind it, because you do not close a window somebody found. The one tile that would not fit anywhere lies at the bottom corner, still waiting. A grid restored badly is more honest than a grid restored well. The next hand can turn the tiles right, or take the window out.
process: I kept Kite's paper field, creases, tile pattern, violet veins, cracked seal and the sky cavity, removed the heap of fallen tiles and the four root cavities, set four tiles back into those cells rotated a quarter or half turn each, outlined every repaired cell with a wide gold seam, and left one tile unplaced at the lower right with a dashed outline marking the open window.
